scope: Worker-startup attribution followed by matched four-CPU versus six-CPU affinity screen under unchanged four-core CPU quota. Current separate-browser native composition; no browser or Rust source changes.

policy.hypothesis: Four-worker captures report frequent throttled quota periods with six allowed CPUs and a four-core bandwidth limit. Restricting actual affinity to four CPUs may improve complete time without more CPU budget. The exact same policy change applies to Playwright.

invariants.candidate: preceding native separate-browser baseline; no source cache

policy.advancement: At least 10% complete candidate reduction in both real applications in both orders, no more than 5% regression in any targeted controlled family. Reference ratios reported at both affinities. No final benchmark policy change without other worker-count and functional/resource validation.
policy.controls: Preflight all five families, four workers, both engines, four-CPU affinity before timings. Existing six-CPU baseline controls remain separately verified.
policy.limits: Diagnostic throttled_usec is aggregate cgroup accounting and is not wall-clock time saved. This is a scheduling-policy experiment, not a browser architectural speedup or final eight-pair acceptance.

startupAttribution.scope: Diagnostic event logging perturbs execution. Parent collection uses within-process monotonic intervals; cross-process chronology uses UTC milliseconds, not per-process hrtime origins. Operation intervals include downstream work and may overlap; they are not CPU or additive critical-path bounds.

earlierClockAttempt.limitation: Pinned Bun hrtime values had process-relative origins. Those earlier records are valid only for within-process intervals and are not used to align worker chronology. Separate corrected-clock captures are used above.

startupAttribution.decision: Worker collection commonly takes about 50 ms in the observed parent intervals, with successor workers starting after the first collection. Framework-only prewarming would require a new explicit assignment/custody boundary; it is not selected as the next large-gain experiment.

limitations: Both application cells must improve at least 10% in both orders and controlled cells must not regress over 5%; the declared gate fails. Do not change benchmark policy or repeat an unchanged larger screen on this basis.
Quota throttled time is aggregated scheduler accounting, not a measure of recoverable wall-clock time; reduced throttling does not prove faster complete work.
Actual policy is captured in the original owner; exhaustive per-thread affinity custody and final resource admission remain unverified.
Four workers only in the matched affinity screen; no new one-worker policy, other-platform or production performance claim.
Stock and custom browser differences remain explicit. Two observations per cell do not satisfy the final eight-pair confidence gate or majority-scenario objective.
No browser/Rust/product implementation changed. The five temporarily instrumented generated JavaScript modules were restored byte-for-byte before all affinity captures.
